result.topic_en: Euler shows for the divisor P = 7 the residue series of geometric progressions with roots 2, 4, 5, and explains that roots less than P suffice, that negative roots may be used, and that the root −a gives the same residues as P − a.
result.transcription:
88 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM

12. Si pro eodem diuiſore $P=7$ radici $a$ alii valores tribuantur, ſeries reſiduorum ſe habebunt vt ſequitur:
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{Progr. geom.}\ 1, 2, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4, 2^5, 2^6, 2^7, 2^8, 2^9 \text{ etc.}\\ \text{Reſidua}\ 1, 2, 4, 1, 2, 4, 1, 2, 4, 1 \text{ etc.}\end{array}\right.$
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{Progr. geom.}\ 1, 4, 4^2, 4^3, 4^4, 4^5, 4^6, 4^7, 4^8, 4^9 \text{ etc.}\\ \text{Reſidua}\ 1, 4, 2, 1, 4, 2, 1, 4, 2, 1 \text{ etc.}\end{array}\right.$
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{Progr. geom.}\ 1, 5, 5^2, 5^3, 5^4, 5^5, 5^6, 5^7, 5^8, 5^9 \text{ etc.}\\ \text{Reſidua}\ 1, 5, 4, 6, 2, 3, 1, 5, 4, 6 \text{ etc.}\end{array}\right.$

13. Vt omnes variationes, quae in ſerie reſiduorum locum habere poſſunt, obtineantur, ſufficit radici $a$ omnes valores diuiſore $P$ minores tribuiſſe; ſi enim loco $a$ ſumatur $a+P$, ex progreſſione geometrica $1, a+P, (a+P)^2, (a+P)^3$ etc. eadem reſiduorum ſeries recurrit, quae ex progreſſione geometrica $1, a, a^2, a^3, a^4$ etc.

14. Quemadmodum in reſiduis etiam numeros negatiuos admittimus (9) vt ea infra ſemiſſem diuiſoris $P$ deprimamus, ita etiam pro radice progreſſionis geometricae $a$ numeros negatiuos aſſumere licet, ac tum habebitur:
$\begin{array}{l}\text{Progr. geom.}\ 1, -a, +a^2, -a^3, +a^4, -a^5, +a^6, -a^7 \text{ etc.}\\ \text{reſidua}\ 1, -\alpha, \beta, -\gamma, \delta, -\varepsilon, \zeta, -\eta \text{ etc.}\end{array}$

15. Sumta autem radice $-a$, eadem reſidua oriuntur, ac ſi radix poneretur $P-a$; vnde patet pro caſibus, quibus radix $a$ ſemiſſem diuiſoris $P$ ſuperat, reſidua ex caſibus quibus eſt $a<\frac{1}{2}P$ facile colligi.

16.

items.quote: Vt omnes variationes, quae in ſerie reſiduorum locum habere poſſunt, obtineantur, ſufficit radici $a$ omnes valores diuiſore $P$ minores tribuiſſe
items.english: To obtain all variations which can occur in the series of residues, it suffices to give the root a all values less than the divisor P.

items.quote: Sumta autem radice $-a$, eadem reſidua oriuntur, ac ſi radix poneretur $P-a$
items.english: Taking the root −a, the same residues arise as if the root were set as P − a.

items.quote: vnde patet pro caſibus, quibus radix $a$ ſemiſſem diuiſoris $P$ ſuperat, reſidua ex caſibus quibus eſt $a<\frac{1}{2}P$ facile colligi.
items.english: Hence it is clear that, for cases where the root a exceeds half the divisor P, the residues are easily deduced from the cases where a < P/2.
